page: Microsoft Azure M16ms is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the MS server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical Intel Xeon 8280M cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz and includes a 38 MB L3 cache. This instance is equipped with 438.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 27.34 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 524 GB SSD, and the instance is premium storage capable. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Performance benchmarks reveal a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, falls in the bottom 10%, indicating weaker single-threaded execution speeds. However, multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth tests, including large-block uncached read and write operations, consistently register in the average range. Database operations, Redis SET performance, and static web serving throughput also achieve average tier results. For machine learning workloads, LLM inference speeds are average for small 135M models but drop to the bottom 25% for medium 7B models.

The primary tradeoff of the M16ms is its modest single-threaded CPU performance relative to its massive memory footprint. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the hardware profile is optimized for memory-intensive workloads that require large datasets to reside in RAM rather than raw compute power. It is highly suitable for large relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, enterprise resource planning applications, and memory-heavy data processing pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure M16ms is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the MS family, powered by an Intel Xeon 8280M processor with 16 dedicated vCPUs and 8 physical cores. It features an exceptionally high memory capacity of 438.0 GB and includes a 524 GB local SSD. While single-core CPU benchmarks place this instance in the bottom 10%, its multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations consistently reach average tiers. The hardware configuration is highly optimized for memory-dense workloads rather than raw single-threaded compute speed. This profile makes the M16ms an appropriate choice for large-scale in-memory databases, caching layers, and enterprise applications requiring substantial RAM capacity without the need for high-frequency CPU performance.
